tax.text: As the PTC is a refundable credit (i.e., a credit with a direct-pay option available), the PTC is outside the scope of ASC 740, Income Taxes (“ASC 740”). Therefore, the Company has analogized the accounting of the PTC to accounting for government grants due to the ability to receive payment for the credit regardless of whether the Company has an income tax liability. Under a government grant model, once it is reasonably assured that the entity will comply with the conditions of the grant, the grant money should be recognized on a systematic basis over the period in which the entity recognizes the related expenses or losses for which the grant money is intended to compensate. The Company recognizes grants once it is probable that both of the following conditions will be met: (1) the Company is eligible to receive the grant and (2) the Company is able to comply with the relevant conditions of the grant.

tax.text: As the PTC is a refundable credit (i.e., a credit with a direct-pay option available), the PTC is outside the scope of ASC 740, Income Taxes (“ASC 740”). Therefore, the Company has analogized the accounting of the PTC to accounting for government grants due to the ability to receive payment for the credit regardless of whether the Company has an income tax liability. Under a government grant model, once it is reasonably assured that the entity will comply with the conditions of the grant, the grant money should be recognized on a systematic basis over the period in which the entity recognizes the related expenses or losses for which the grant money is intended to compensate. The Company recognizes grants once it is probable that both of the following conditions will be met: (1) the Company is eligible to receive the grant and (2) the Company is able to comply with the relevant conditions of the grant.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Additionally, 14.3% of our total consolidated revenues were associated with our second largest customer.

As of December 31, 2025, one customer individually exceeded 10% of total consolidated accounts receivable with a balance of $ 48.9 million, or 36.3 %, of the Company’s consolidated accounts receivable.

As of December 31, 2024, one customer individually exceeded 10% of total consolidated accounts receivable with a balance of $ 38.5 million, or 24.5 %, of the Company’s consolidated accounts receivable.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, two customers individually exceeded 10% of total consolidated revenues.
One customer accounted for $ 171.8 million, or 24.2 %, and one customer accounted for $ 101.7 million, or 14.3 %, of total consolidated revenues.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, two customers individually exceeded 10% of total consolidated revenues.
One customer accounted for $ 104.6 million, or 16.6 %, and one customer accounted for $ 90.9 million, or 14.4 %, of total consolidated revenues.
For the year ended December 31, 2023, two customers individually exceeded 10% of total consolidated revenues.
One customer accounted for $ 209.0 million, or 23.4 %, and one customer accounted for $ 97.0 million, or 10.9 %, of total consolidated revenues.

Any future determination as to the payment of dividends will depend upon capital requirements and limitations imposed by our debt agreements, if any, and such other factors as our Board may consider.
